newsitem.title: UK: Clyde counterbid hopes fade after Gulf raid.
newsitem.headline: Clyde counterbid hopes fade after Gulf raid.

text.p: Hopes of a counterbid emerging for Clyde Petroleum Plc evaporated on Tuesday as predator Gulf Canada raised its stake in the British oil exploration and production firm to about 27 percent, analysts said.
Turnover in Clyde was over 82.4 million shares in late afternoon trade after Gulf Canada had entered the market in a well-timed bid to make its hostile 120 pence per share offer succeed, they added.
Gulf's buying activity comes after recent steep falls in crude oil prices which may have driven investors into the arms of the Canadian bidder.
"If a white knight comes in now they have blown it," said one leading analyst.
"They should have stepped in immediately after Gulf raised its offer and stop investors selling to Gulf," he added.
Gulf launched a 105 pence per share bid on December 18 and raised the offer to 120 pence last week.
Four institutional shareholders -- Schroders Plc, PDFM Limited, Capital Group Companies Inc and Norwich Union hold more than 50 percent of Clyde.
But after today's buying, Gulf now no longer needs to convince all of these major shareholders in order to gain control over Clyde.
"Gulf is playing on fears now that there won't be a white knight, that one or two of the big shareholders will accept and that the whole sector will go down as oil prices slip," another analyst said.
Chances of Gulf's offer succeeding had increased substantially after today, he added.
"They only need support of one or two of the major shareholders and then they've got it basically," he said.
